cells.tense: You're tending what's growing, and it isn't costing you the way it used to.
cells.ask: Offer: let one finished thing go so a new one has somewhere to land — and notice the room it leaves, not the gap.
cells.core:
You've got the weight and the warm hands at the same time. You hold your own form while something else takes shape, and neither one is eating the other. The load is real and the grip is loose enough — that's the whole trick, and you're doing it. Nothing around you is going hungry and nothing around you is being propped up past what it needs.

What that's worth: you can tell when a thing is done and set it down without calling the setting-down a loss. That's the next thing this balance can feed — room opens where something finished used to sit, and you trust it to fill.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold the load and still let something go.
cells.place: under a load you're still holding up

cells.tense: You're bracing for a future where they'll finally be alright, and you're carrying them there ahead of time.
cells.ask: Offer: imagine one outcome you can't control, sit in the not-knowing for a day, and let the next move come after — what's yours to do shows up clearer.
cells.core:
In a good week, you carry people and they still walk on their own. You're the wall they lean on for a minute, not the hand that moves their feet. The holding makes them steadier, and you come out of it with something left over, not scraped down.

Nobody asked you to take on what hasn't happened yet, and you've already picked it up. Something's going wrong down the road, so you get there first — checking, steering, doing more than you were asked — and the people you're trying to grow end up small in a room you've crowded. Enough light for the next step is enough. You don't need the whole road mapped to put one foot down.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying people past where they need to walk.
cells.place: under a load you're still holding up

cells.tense: You're still standing at a point where tending something felt like too much to ask.
cells.ask: Offer: name one thing you actually want to see grow, and put a small amount of energy toward it this week — the wanting does the work; you don't have to push.
cells.core:
The strong picture here is a load you chose and a thing you're growing beside it — you hold what's yours and you feed what matters, and both stay alive. The carrying has a why, and the why has hands on it.

The load is still there and the tending isn't. Nothing around you is growing, and you've been calling that standing on your own. Being unavailable reads as independence, but it isn't holding anything up — it's just not reaching.

You don't have to push a starved part back to life. What gets you moving is letting something pull you — a thing you want, not a thing you owe. Wanting is the tap. Turn it on small and the current comes through.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing's growing because you've stopped wanting anything to.
cells.place: under a load you're still holding up

cells.tense: You're already carrying people, already the one they come to, and you don't call it caring.
cells.ask: Offer: pick one thing you do for someone and call it what it is — not duty, not just practicality — and let that be enough reason to keep it or drop it.
cells.core:
At its steadiest, this looks like a load you chose and know the shape of — you know what you're holding and who you're holding it for, and the giving leaves you with something rather than down to nothing. The hands are open and the reason is yours.

People lean on you, and you've folded that into the furniture. It's not a decision you made; it's a role that landed and you kept carrying it. You feel used up. They feel held.

Nobody's asking you to feel more. The question is whether you keep holding this by default or by choice. One honest look at what's yours to give and what's just been assumed tells you whether it stays or goes — and either answer is clean.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding things up and you've never claimed it.
cells.place: under a load you're still holding up
